title: Plan rows are never pruned and each stores about 130 KB of JSON: the workspace file grows about 12.5 MB per site per day (4.6 GB per site-year), copied daily x14, and plan-history reads slow down linearly
label: spec-mismatch
url: data/companies/<company>.db; GET /api/sites/:id/genset, POST /api/reports, the tick's alerts
steps:
1) Read-only dbstat on .scratch/data/companies/6321e32a-d640-44b9-8cf3-bf06164b2e0c.db.
2) grep 'DELETE FROM plans' in backend/gridlytics: only demo removal and site deletion, no retention.
3) Run perf-live/plans_growth.py: a scratch file holding 2,500, 5,000 and 10,000 realistic plan rows of one site (cloned from a real demo plan); time the queries plans.py and reports.py run.
expected: Spec Part 3.3 retention (EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md line 278): steps and slots of superseded plans are kept 90 days, then only for the first plan of each hour, the plan active at each step and applied plans. File growth is bounded, and plan reads do not grow with history length.
actual:
Every 15-minute plan keeps its full steps JSON: 644 B per step x 192 steps, with the keys repeated in every step.
- Today: plans are 69.72 MB of the 70.6 MB file (528 rows; avg steps 126,084 B, slots 3,602 B, summary 1,107 B).
- Growth: 96 plans per site per day x about 131 KB = about 12.5 MB per site per day, 4.6 GB per site-year, about 228 GB per year at 50 sites, all in one company file.
- backups.daily_all copies that file every day and keeps 14 copies (KEEP=14): at 50 sites a 250 GB disk fills in about a month.
- Synthetic file: 2,500 / 5,000 / 10,000 plans (26 / 52 / 104 days) = 328 / 656 / 1,311 MB.
- plans.active_at took 12.9 / 28.7 / 51.5 ms. Its query uses the (site_id, generated_at) index, then sorts by belief_time ('USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY'), so it scans the site's whole history: about 180 ms per call at a year.
- active_at is called up to 16 times per tick per advisory non-demo site (alerts._peak_unconfirmed), once per outage (alerts.evaluate), and once per genset run on GET /genset (polled every 60 s).
- The monthly report's per-day plan-id query (substr(belief_time,1,10)) took 90 / 190 / 433 ms, so about 1.5 s per report at a year.
evidence:
dbstat: plans 69.72 MB / 528 rows; companies/backup holds 51.5 MB and 59.9 MB daily copies.
plans_growth.py output: {plans:10000, file_mb:1311, active_at_ms:51.5, report_month_plan_ids_ms:432.9}.
Code: plans.py:455-467 (insert, no prune); plans.py:603-622 (active_at); alerts.py:91-92 and 132; routes_telemetry.py:323; reports.py:152; backups.py:26,86-87.
Spec: line 278. Tracker: DAT-09 is [~].

title: Every site page polls /now every 30 s only for its header, and /now re-reads 30 days of 1-minute data (battery.state) on each call: the API caps at about 7 /now requests per second
label: bug
steps:
1) Open any site page. The header's useSiteNow (frontend/src/lib/use-meta.ts:44, components/layout/site-header.tsx:14) polls GET /api/sites/:id/now every 30 s and reads only site.tier, control and last_data.
2) Time /now x3 as owner:
   - Faisalabad p50 0.120 s / p95 0.142 s; Karachi 0.121 / 0.126; Lahore 0.131 / 0.142; RYK 0.127 / 0.132.
   - Site 22029dfe45a7 (27 days inside the 30-day window): 0.197 / 0.227. Its /battery took 0.217 s.
3) cProfile on a DB copy: battery.state is 108 ms of the call. It runs telemetry.minute_grid(now-30 d), and raw() selects all 25 columns and builds each array from a Python list comprehension.
4) perf-live/concurrency.py with 8 concurrent callers on /now.
expected: The header's control state and last-data stamp come from a couple of indexed reads (milliseconds). The battery estimate is computed once per minute or per tick and cached, not on every request.
actual:
Each open site tab costs 0.13-0.22 s of the single API worker every 30 s. The battery page computes battery.state twice per refresh (/now and /battery).
- Throughput: 1 caller 7.5 req/s; 8 callers 7.3 req/s with p50 0.68 s, p95 2.96 s, max 4.3 s.
- For the 27-day site: 4.7 req/s, p95 3.45 s, max 5.1 s.
- So about 140-220 open site tabs saturate the worker before any other work.
- In page loads, /now took 0.30-0.37 s while the page's other calls ran.
evidence:
perf-live/routes-owner.json; concurrency output ('/api/sites/6d4db49bf87e/now threads=8 n=91 rps=7.3 p50=0.680 p95=2.964').
Code: routes_sites.py:398-424 (battery.state at 414); battery.py:21; telemetry.py:362-374 (raw) and 377-400 (minute_grid); routes_telemetry.py:281.

title: Every telemetry read takes the telemetry file's write lock (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), so all reads and writes of a company's telemetry run one at a time
label: bug
url: every route that reads telemetry (/now, /battery, /telemetry, export.csv, /outages), edge ingest, CSV upload, the tick
steps:
1) Read telemetry.connect (telemetry.py:102-113): it runs con.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE') for every caller, including latest(), first_ts(), raw() and export_csv().
2) On a copy of the company files, run 3 threads:
   - A holds telemetry.connect() over SELECT * FROM minute plus 1 s.
   - B calls telemetry.latest('e9941b41c70b') 0.2 s later.
   - C makes a plain WAL read of the same row.
3) Upload a 60-day CSV (8.8 MB) while polling a telemetry-reading route (/telemetry/quality) and a route that reads no telemetry (/alerts/counts).
expected: Readers use deferred (read) transactions: in WAL mode they never wait for each other or for a writer. Only writers take BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
actual:
Thread B's 0.2 ms read waited 1.233 s behind A. The plain WAL read (C) took 0.000 s.
- export_csv formats the whole CSV inside the lock (telemetry.py:583-591): the 32-day export (4.5 MB) holds it for 0.47 s.
- /now, charts, battery reads, the tick's forecast reads, CSV ingest and every edge batch therefore queue on one lock. A holder longer than busy_timeout (30 s) makes the others fail with 'database is locked'.
- During the upload, the telemetry route peaked at 1.26 s against 0.82 s for the route that reads no telemetry.

title: A 23.5 MB CSV upload takes 14 s, raises the API process's memory by 544 MB (23x the file) and stalls other users' requests to about 1 s
label: bug
steps:
1) Create the scratch site 'AUDIT perf upload' (22029dfe45a7).
2) Generate a 1-minute logger CSV with perf-live/make_csv.py: 160 days, 230,400 rows, 17 columns, 23,470,163 bytes.
3) POST it as text/csv with ?tz_offset_h=0&file_name=perf.csv, while polling GET /api/alerts/counts every 0.25 s and the API's VmRSS (perf-live/upload_test.py).
expected: Bounded memory and a streamed or chunked parse (spec Part 2.8: untrusted CSV parsed with size and time caps). Other users' requests are unaffected.
actual:
200 after 14.16 s.
- API RSS went from 212 MB to a 756 MB peak, and was still 357 MB afterwards.
- /alerts/counts (8 ms when idle) took 0.98, 1.06, 0.89, 0.74 and 0.44 s during the parse: pure Python holding the GIL in the single worker.
- Three concurrent uploads at the 25 MB limit would add about 1.6 GB.
- Cause: routes_telemetry.py:66-114 decodes and parses the whole file for the date-window check. telemetry.import_csv then decodes it again into a list of 230k dicts (telemetry.py:283-305) before ingest, and aggregates every day.
- A year of 1-minute data (about 54 MB at 102 B per row) needs 3 or more files because of MAX_BODY 25 MB (api.py:100).
evidence:
perf-live/upload-160d.json: {seconds:14.16, rows:230400, rss_before_mb:212, rss_peak_mb:756, rss_after_mb:357, other_requests_max_s:1.058}.
Code: routes_telemetry.py:66-114, 124-131 and 146-170; telemetry.py:273-330.

title: Re-solve, resume and savings recompute run the solver inside the HTTP request: 3.6 s measured, up to 30 s for a solve, and up to 62 five-second solves for one recompute
label: bug
steps:
1) As owner, POST /api/sites/9df495def65d/plan/solve (AUDIT farm owner 375, which has a genset).
2) Read routes_plans.py:76-89 and 187-200: demo.advance plus plans.tick run in the request.
3) Read optimise.solve_with_policy (optimise.py:840-860) and solve()'s shed-rule re-solve and threshold repair (optimise.py:~560-590).
4) On a DB copy, time verify.compute_range for 14 days per demo site (the work of POST /savings/recompute).
expected: Work that can take seconds runs as a job: answer 202, then the page polls (jobs.py, lifted with progress and cancel, is unused). Or it is bounded well under a proxy's read timeout.
actual:
The solve answered after 3.59 s (solve_seconds 3.517; 3,071 variables; 766 binaries). The same site's scheduled solve took 6.91 s at 12:30 on an idle machine.
- The code allows three 10 s limits per tick, so up to 30 s or more per click.
- /savings/recompute runs a perfect-foresight MILP per day (verify.py:801, time_limit 5 s): 14 days took 3.4-4.6 s per demo site (0.25-0.33 s per day). The allowed 62 days is about 15-20 s, and about 5 minutes worst case, in one request. Behind a 60 s proxy timeout it fails while the work continues.
- The solve releases the GIL: other requests stayed at 34 ms or less during it.
evidence:
Live answer {'status': 'active', 'plan_id': 'f552fb48573c', 'solve_seconds': 3.517} after 3.59 s; runs row 9df495def65d at the 12:30 tick: solve_s 6.905.
Copy timings: 'Karachi savings recompute 14 days 4.645 s'.
Code: routes_plans.py:76-89, 187-200; routes_savings.py:46-56; verify.py:801, 987-994; jobs.py (no caller).

title: Tick timing cannot be observed: no tick or per-site duration is logged, and a manual re-solve overwrites the scheduled run's row
label: bug
steps:
1) Read the runs table read-only: SELECT tick, min(started), max(finished) GROUP BY tick.
2) Compare with the audit table: the 07:45 tick of 6132568cd101 'started' at 07:59:21, the same second as 'Demo Owner re-solved the plan'.
3) I ran POST /plan/solve on 9df495def65d at about 12:22. The 12:15 tick then shows max(finished) 12:22:06, although the scheduler finished at 12:15:28.
4) Read scheduler._all (scheduler.py:57-62): it drops tick_company's {sites, failed}.
expected: Each scheduled tick records its own start, end and per-site durations, separately from manual re-solves, and logs a line per tick. Failed sites are recorded too.
actual:
runs has primary key (site_id, tick), and both the scheduler and the solve route write it with INSERT OR REPLACE (plans.py:440, 466), so a re-solve in the same quarter erases the tick's timing. This made the 07:45 and 08:00 ticks look 841 s and 397 s long.

Sites whose tick raises leave no run row at all: 1d0dfac8457a and 70492545d4ec raise NoTariffVersion every tick.

No duration is logged anywhere.

title: The 15-minute tick runs every site of every company in one thread inside the API process; its per-site cost grows with history and a genset site may take three 10 s limits
label: feature-gap
steps:
1) Watch the live ticks (perf-live/tickwatch.jsonl, polling /now and /fleet every second) and read their runs rows.
2) Profile one tick on a DB copy with each phase wrapped (perf-live/prof_tick.py).
expected: A tick's length is bounded well under the quarter and does not grow with history. The documented ~90 sites per core holds, or the solves move to workers.
actual:
Live ticks: 12:15 took 8 s, 12:30 took 10 s (10 sites each). At 12:30 the AUDIT farm alone solved in 6.91 s on an idle machine (3.5-3.6 s in other runs; limit 10 s).

Copy profile: 12 sites in 8.8 s. Each demo site costs 0.8-0.93 s:
- forecast.issue 0.26-0.38 s
- battery.state x2 0.23-0.31 s (reads 30 days, so this doubles as data ages)
- build_problem 0.14-0.29 s
- alerts.evaluate 0.12-0.17 s
- solve 0.03-0.30 s
At a year of plans, alerts' active_at adds about 3 s per advisory site.

One thread uses one core, whatever the machine. With max_instances=1 and coalesce, an overrun skips the next quarter.

During the 12:15 tick, /now rose to 0.36 s (baseline p50 0.137 s) and /fleet to 0.49 s (0.07 s).
evidence:
Runs: tick 12:30 10 sites 12:30:20-12:30:30, 9df495def65d solve_s 6.905.
prof_tick1.log 'TOTAL 8.77'.
Code: scheduler.py:19-35, 64-67 (docstring: 'at about 90 sites per core the solves move to workers'); optimise.py comment 'A tick stays within three limits'.
HANDOFF.md:262 (plan quality depends on CPU load).
